indigo-galaxy · exedev · 2026-11-25 01:21–01:37 UTC · Claude Code 2.1.331 · agents: claude-opus-5-5, effort xhigh · feat/stall @ 7caf0a9 · PR branch feat/resume · one take, unedited

A real crash, twice: ./launch.sh --resume brought the team back, and it finished

In one live run of four Claude Opus 5.5 agents (xhigh) on the bundled seven-statement task, I killed the gateway with SIGKILL and the run's tmux session twice: once with 6 of 7 statements on main (down 3 min 7 s), once while h1 had an uncommitted draft of the last statement (down 1 min 16 s). Each time boss.sh status said INTERRUPTED and a plain ./launch.sh refused. ./launch.sh --resume moved the deadline by the time down (187.8 s and 76.4 s: 1.0 s and 0.5 s more than measured from the kill, inside one heartbeat) and kept the board, main and the workspaces byte-identical. It restarted each agent from its rejoining brief. The draft landed unchanged (same sha256), and the run finished 7 of 7 after 6 min 6 s of running time against a 45-minute budget. verify.py: 7 PASS.

Findings

  1. Durations shown after a resume count the outage as running time. After the run, boss.sh status (and the board window) said RUN COMPLETE in 10.5 min, which is DONE − started. 4 min 24 s of that was down time, which the deadline gave back; the team ran 6 min 6 s. report.py does the same ("time used 10m 29s of 45 min", report.py:262), so a resumed run looks closer to its budget than it is. template/harness/board.py:41
  2. While a run is down, the boss still sees the clocks running. At 01:27:36, 84 s into the outage, boss.sh status said time left: 40 min and stall clock: 1 of 30 min (board.py:51). Both are given back by --resume, which then said "time left: 42 min". Nothing in the INTERRUPTED output says the time down will be returned, so a boss deciding between resume and archive could misread how much time is left. Minor. template/harness/board.py:33
  3. A resume right after a crash is refused for up to 10 s, by guesswork. 5 s after kill 2, --resume refused: "the heartbeat is 6 s old: a gateway may still be serving this directory". The refusal is safe and correct. But the gateway holds an exclusive flock on config.json while it serves (gateway.py:662), and trying that lock would answer the question for certain, without the 10-second wait. A suggestion, not a bug. template/harness/runstate.py:110

Not covered

  • A real power loss or reboot. Only the gateway (SIGKILL) and the tmux session were killed, so the page cache and the disk stayed. The board survived in WAL mode, but nothing tested lost writes or fsync.
  • A crash in the middle of a merge (state/ci/ worktree left behind; design.md says main moves by one atomic ref update). Neither kill hit a merge.
  • A run that was paused, out of time or stalled when it died (ended, resumed paused): not run live.
  • A removed helper across a resume, and a helper that does not come back (the lead reopening its claims after 10 minutes): every helper came back, so the reopen path was only announced by the lead, not used.
  • A crash during the lead's setup, before announce exists.
  • TEAM_REMOTE_CONTROL=1 with --resume.

Audit trail

One take, lifecycle.cast; no take was discarded. It ran from 01:21:20 to 01:37:25 UTC. Every keystroke in it came from rec.sh type/run, sent by me (an agent); no person typed.

Expected values and tolerances were written to expected.md at 01:20 UTC, before the take; chapter 1 shows its timestamp. The pre-kill values for each crash were written by crash.sh (snapshot prekill-N) before the kill.

Crash 1 was not as tight as planned. watch-team.sh fired at 01:25:21 when 2 statements had landed, but crash.sh's first snapshot took 51 s: my procs.sh forked twice per /proc entry (931 processes, about 40 s a scan). Meanwhile four more statements landed, and the kill came at 01:26:12 with 6 of 7 on main. So prekill-1 is not the state right before kill 1. The state at the kill is down-1, read after every writer was dead (no process of the run left, gateway SIGKILLed; the gateway log's last record is 01:26:11.217, before the kill). Before crash 2 I replaced it with a one-pass procs.py; prekill-2 was written 1.3 s before kill 2. The line "processes under run/ after 1s: none" in crash 1 means "at the first scan", which itself took about 30 s.

harness/boss.sh trust was run right after the launch and after each resume, as SKILL.md says. After the launch it answered yes in lead, h1, h2 and h3; after both resumes it reported "started without a prompt" for all four (the folders were already trusted). No other prompt was answered for the user. I sent nothing to the agents: no boss.sh say, no keys into their windows. The seven team msg messages were the agents' own.

The take's shell was started with my session's CLAUDECODE, CLAUDE_CODE_* and ANTHROPIC_* variables removed (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR kept), so selftest.sh's claude -p ran as a plain session. The team's tmux session takes its environment from the default tmux server. Its windows were 188×66 (the server's window-size latest).

The brief points to a section "Things to know before demoing the live team" in proof/README.md; that section does not exist (the README ends with shoot.py). I followed "Watching another tmux session" and read the team only with tmux capture-pane -p.

Outside the take: one read-only sqlite3 -readonly look at the board at 01:25:34 and jq reads of records/gateway.jsonl while the run went on; the screenshots (shoot.py, bin/frames.py, which seeks the same asciinema-player as this page); bin/readback.sh; two scratch report runs (escape-test/, regen-test/) on copies of the archived records.

Clean-up: ./teardown.sh --archive stopped the session and the gateway at 01:36:37. At 01:37:20 tmux ls listed no demo-lifecycle session and procs.py found no process of the run. The two scratch copies (fresh/, stopped-copy/) were purged and deleted inside the take. Nothing I started is still running. Left on disk under /home/exedev/codes/tat-dev/demo/lifecycle: run/ (template files, report.html, harness/__pycache__), archive-out/, unpack/, clone/, venv/, evidence/, frames/, shots/, pages-src/.

Redactions: none were needed. A grep of the cast and of the pages for API keys, tokens, ~/.claude and ~/.ssh paths and e-mail addresses found nothing.
